title: Healthcare’s Next Era Is Continuous: Key Takeaways From HLTH 2026
summary: The challenge for HCOs in 2027 is to turn newly available intelligence into greater consumer confidence. This means helping consumers understand what's happening, deciding what to do next, and connecting with the right human expertise when it matters most.
body_markdown:
The challenge for HCOs in 2027 is to turn newly available intelligence into greater consumer confidence. This means helping consumers understand what’s happening, deciding what to do next, and connecting with the right human expertise when it matters most.


Healthcare has spent decades talking about moving from


[paying for sick care](https://www.forrester.com/report/breaking-the-sickness-revenue-cycle/RES189757?ref_search=3208316_1795183415081) to more emphasis on prevention. At


[HLTH 2026](https://hlth.com/insights/articles/hlth-usa-2026-the-age-of-intelligent-health-is-here-buckle-up) , it felt like the combination of technology capabilities and adoption, along with


[consumer empowerment over their data](https://www.fiercehealthcare.com/health-tech/hhs-finalizes-updates-hipaa-privacy-rule-ease-patient-access-health-information?utm_medium=email&utm_source=nl&utm_campaign=HC-NL-FierceHealthPayer&oly_enc_id=4467F5979323E1I) , may finally start to make this industry ambition a possibility. Presentations, conversations, announcements, and even the types of products showcased in the expo all leaned in this direction. Just imagine if we could continuously understand our health and act before problems become crises?


**The big opportunity now: redefining prevention.**


The future of prevention is


[an always-on experience](https://www.forrester.com/report/redefining-healthcare-in-an-always-on-digital-ecosystem/RES181719?ref_search=3208316_1795185567203) that helps consumers understand, decide, act, and improve. It moves healthcare from episodic encounters (think annual screenings, reminders to exercise and eat better, etc.) instead toward continuous health management.


But (and it’s a big “but”) first reimbursement must catch up to incentivize for avoided events, not just sick care. With the traditional health insurance model


[under growing pressure](https://www.forrester.com/report/forresters-us-health-insurers-brand-experience-index-rankings-2026/RES199328?ref_search=3208316_1795185607754) and more consumers choosing to go uninsured, healthcare may finally be reaching a tipping point to lean fully into prevention and revamp the operational aspects.


**Here are the big takeaways that stood out for our team at HLTH 2026:**


1. **Prevention is being redefined.** Wearables and diagnostics can surface risks earlier, but consumers are still left wondering what it means or what to do. Oura’s


[planned acquisition of Counsel Health](https://www.counselhealth.com/newsroom/oura-to-acquire-counsel-health-advancing-vision-for-more-connected-personalized-healthcare) is a market signal of this broader shift. By combining continuous biometric data, AI, and clinical access, consumers can turn insights into action.


2. **Policy remains the immovable object.** Where they obtain care is becoming increasingly irrelevant to consumers, but it still matters enormously to reimbursement, creating a mismatch between where healthcare is headed, along with how and who pays for it. Healthcare organizations (HCOs) pursuing more emphasis on prevention must redesign incentives, experiences, workflows, reimbursement, and outcome measurement around keeping people healthy.


3. **Longevity is challenging healthcare’s assumptions about aging.** Peter Stern, CEO and President of Peloton, notes that Peloton members 50 years and older log 45% more workouts than younger members. Not surprisingly, the AgeTech Collaborative with AARP showcased technologies built for a 50+ population that increasingly wants to actively manage their health and healthspan, not simply receive care. HCOs that continue to equate aging with sickness will miss a growing market of consumers who are willing to invest in longevity AND staying healthy longer.


4. **AI is moving from answering questions to extending the care team.** AI can expand scarce clinical capacity by monitoring patients continuously, managing routine interventions, and escalating when a clinician needs to step in. As AI becomes a more continuous part of health management, Apple’s 200,000-person


[study with OpenEvidence](https://www.fiercehealthcare.com/ai-and-machine-learning/hlth26-apple-kicks-new-study-examine-use-ai-chatbots-health?utm_medium=email&utm_source=nl&utm_campaign=HC-NL-FierceHealthTech&oly_enc_id=4467F5979323E1I) aims to better understand how consumers use and respond to AI-generated health guidance, putting trust at the center of adoption. This is critical as


[medical deserts](https://www.forrester.com/blogs/its-not-a-mirage-we-need-a-way-out-of-the-medical-desert/?ref_search=3208316_1795184072215) persist across the US. For example, one conversation highlighted the impact on congestive heart failure (CHF). Nearly


[half of US counties](https://www.acc.org/About-ACC/Press-Releases/2024/07/08/18/25/Almost-Half-of-US-Counties-Have-No-Cardiologists-Despite-Higher-Prevalence-of-CV-Risk-Factors-Mortality) lack a practicing cardiologist, while


[roughly 1,500 board-certified advanced heart failure and transplant cardiologists](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S3050661126000559) serve the entire country. AI could extend that scarce expertise, extending the reach of these human specialists. However, trust and strong guardrails are essential to clinician and patient adoption.


5. **Diagnostics are a validation layer, with limits.** At home diagnostics support was a prominent focus this year, from the free blood test coupon and vial in your swag bag to a diagnostics section that nearly doubled in size from past years. Most vendors offer white labeled service capabilities or analytical support for clinician practices or organizations that don’t have their own lab facilities, but some shared they have intentions of


[expanding into the DTC market](https://www.forrester.com/report/predictions-2027-healthcare/RES202220?ref_search=3208316_1795185292019) . Available does not mean attainable, as most DTC options carry a high price tag and


[may create new disparities for vulnerable populations](https://www.forrester.com/report/predictions-2027-healthcare/RES202220?ref_search=3208316_1795185292019) .


6. **Women’s health was a dominant theme.** The conversation on Women’s health has graduated from a niche digital-health category to a horizontal healthcare strategy. At HLTH 2026 it showed up in discussions about AI, benefits, care delivery, longevity, and investment rather than being confined to just fertility and femtech. HCOs should


[stop treating women’s health as a specialty strategy](https://www.forrester.com/blogs/the-business-case-for-investing-in-womens-health/?ref_search=3208316_1795185485177) and start designing their core products and experiences around it.


7. **Clinical research needs to become faster and more representative.** At HLTH, ARPA-H Chief Medical Officer Rafid Fadul highlighted the need for speed in growing global competition for biotech innovation. China now accounts for roughly 30% of the global biopharma R&D pipeline. ARPA-H’s SURPASS program aims to tackle this head-on by building out shared research infrastructure, streamlined processes, AI, simulation, and more distributed trial sites to make research faster, less expensive, and accessible beyond major academic medical centers (AMCs).


8. **Human in the loop must not become human in the way.** A panel discussed that human oversight should add clinical value, not turn clinicians into software validators or liability shields expected to fill every AI gap. Panelists emphasized that meaningful oversight depends on thoughtful design, targeted training, and realistic expectations about where humans can add value across vast amounts of data. With no clear consensus yet, HCOs still must define when clinicians should intervene, what they need to know, and who is accountable.
